Because \(T_{ijkl}=T_{jikl}\), the value depends only on the unordered pair \(\{i,j\}\).  
Similarly, because \(T_{ijkl}=T_{ijlk}\), the value depends only on the unordered pair \(\{k,l\}\).

For indices \(1,2,3,4\), the number of unordered pairs is

\[
\binom{4}{2}+4=6+4=10.
\]

Thus the symmetries in \(i,j\) and \(k,l\) reduce the tensor to a \(10\times 10\) matrix \(A\), whose entries correspond to the pairs \((\{i,j\},\{k,l\})\).

The remaining condition is

\[
T_{ijkl}=-T_{klij},
\]

which in terms of \(A\) says

\[
A_{pq}=-A_{qp}.
\]

So \(A\) is skew-symmetric. A skew-symmetric \(10\times 10\) matrix has zero diagonal entries, and its independent entries are the entries above the diagonal. Hence the number of independent components is

\[
\binom{10}{2}=\frac{10\cdot 9}{2}=45.
\]

\[
\boxed{45}
\]
